entries.text: This is done by first pressing the DATA rocker on the UFC and then the SEL rocker until DTS is displayed on the third line of the HUD data block. If DTS is not selected, the elevation will be based on the steerpoint. If based on steerpoint and the steerpoint is at a higher elevation than where the CCIP gun sight is pointed, you will get a CCIP INVALID error. Slant range greatly affects gun effectiveness. As the rounds come out of the gun, they will gradually disperse and lose velocity. Increased dispersion and loss of velocity reduce the accuracy and effectiveness of the gun.
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Gun Employment > Gunsights > 4/8/12 Gun Reticle

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Gun Employment > Gunsights > 4/8/12 Gun Reticle (4)
entries.text: Effective engagement range generally ranges from .5 to 2 miles slant range. For tanks, .5 miles should be maximum range, and you should attack from behind the target where its armor is weakest using CM. If the target is moving, you may want to use the moving target indices on the CCIP Gun Reticle. They assume lead for a moving target at a constant speed of 20 knots perpendicular. For example: if a target is moving left to right at an estimated 10 knots, place target halfway between the pipper and left moving target indices before firing.
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Gun Employment > Gunsights > 4/8/12 Gun Reticle

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Gun Employment > Gunsights > 4/8/12 Gun Reticle (5)
entries.text: When lining up a shot, be careful to avoid target fixation. Target fixation can lead to you not noticing an unseen threat or pressing the attack too close. Don’t make yourself an easy target for the machine gun on the top of that tank!

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Gun Employment > Gun Use (1)
entries.text: When engaging with the gun in a strafing attack, you will want to keep the following points in mind: To accurately use CCIP gun sights, the aircraft must know the elevation of the aim point. This is most often done by selecting DTS elevation. This is done by first pressing the DATA rocker on the UFC and then the SEL rocker until DTS is displayed on the third line of the HUD data block. If DTS is not selected, the elevation will be based on the steerpoint.
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Gun Employment > Gun Use

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Gun Employment > Gun Use (2)
entries.text: If based on steerpoint and the steerpoint is at a higher elevation than where the CCIP gun sight is pointed, you will get a CCIP INVALID error. Slant range greatly affects gun effectiveness. As the rounds come out of the gun, they will gradually disperse and lose velocity. Increased dispersion and loss of velocity reduce the accuracy and effectiveness of the gun. Effective engagement range generally ranges from .5 to 2 miles slant range. For tanks, .5 miles should be maximum range, and you should attack from behind the target where its armor is weakest using CM.
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Gun Employment > Gun Use

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Gun Employment > Gun Use (3)
entries.text: If the target is moving, you may want to use the moving target indices on the CCIP Gun Reticle. They assume lead for a moving target at a constant speed of 20 knots perpendicular. For example: if a target is moving left to right at an estimated 10 knots, place target halfway between the pipper and left moving target indices before firing. When lining up a shot, be careful to avoid target fixation. Target fixation can lead to you not noticing an unseen threat or pressing the attack too close. Don’t make yourself an easy target for the machine gun on the top of that tank!
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Gun Employment > Gun Use

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Gun Employment > Gun Use (4)
entries.text: Once you have reached the minimum attack range, break off in both the horizontal and vertical to avoid hostile return fire. You may also wish to release flares in case an infrared-SAM near the enemy target has been launched at you, but you did not see it. Prior to the strafing attack, you may want to track the target using the targeting pod so that you can perform a battle damage assessment while coming off the target. Be careful not to spot your target though! If the expected target is enemy infantry, it is best to load the aircraft with an HEI gun load.
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Gun Employment > Gun Use

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Gun Employment > Gun Use > Gun Strafe Not Using Precision Attitude Control (PAC) (1)
entries.text: When engaging a target with the gun and the GUN/PAC switch set to GUNARM, the PAC will not be used. As such, you will want to keep the following points in mind for a successful strafing attack: Armored/fortified targets are best attacked from a High Angle Strafe in order to increase round density on target. The further away you engage, the lower the round density on the target will be. Generally, conduct a strafe between 2 and .5nm. For heavily armored targets like tanks, it is best to fire between .5 and 1 nm.
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Gun Employment > Gun Use > Gun Strafe Not Using Precision Attitude Control (PAC)

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Gun Employment > Gun Use > Gun Strafe Not Using Precision Attitude Control (PAC) (2)
entries.text: Area targets or lightly armored targets can be attacked in a Low Angle Strafe due to the increased round dispersion over an elongated area.
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Gun Employment > Gun Use > Gun Strafe Not Using Precision Attitude Control (PAC)

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Gun Employment > Gun Use > Gun Strafe Using PAC
entries.text: PAC assists by stabilizing the aircraft during strafing and allowing much greater round density on target because the pitch and yaw will be controlled during gunfire to keep the rounds from walking from the initial target point. PAC does this by applying elevator and rudder control through the SAS to stabilize the aircraft’s nose during gun fire.
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Gun Employment > Gun Use > Gun Strafe Using PAC

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Gun Employment > Gun Use > CCIP INVALID HUD Message
entries.text:
If the target is at an elevation higher than the current aircraft altitude (target on a hill higher than your current altitude for instance), the system cannot generate proper target altitude and a “CCIP INVALID” message will appear on the HUD. To attack such a target accurately, you have two options:
• Increase altitude above target altitude
• Switch to 4/8/12 Gun Reticle or 4000-Foot Wind Corrected Gun Cross

entries.text:
There are three release settings available for rockets on the Control Page.
• Release Type (OSB 6). Cycle this option to choose between four release types:
• SGL (Singles). Each press of the weapon release button will launch a single rocket.
• PRS (Pairs). Each press of the weapon release button will launch a single rocket from two different pods.
• RIP SGL (Ripple Singles). Each press of the weapon release button will launch the number of rockets specified in the RIP QTY (Ripple Quantity) setting.
• RIP PRS (Ripple Pairs).

• Ripple Quantity (OSB 8). If either RIP SGL or RIP PRS are selected as the Release Type, you may use this to set the number of rockets to release in each ripple.
• Release Mode (OSB 10). Select to release rocket in CCIP or CCRP release modes. This setting, along with being assigned to the HUD rotary, will determine if the profile is selected in the CCRP or CCIP rotary.

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Unguided Rocket Employment > Unguided Rocket CCIP Use (1)
entries.text:
With a rocket profile selected and configured, and the Master Arm switch set to ARM, you can put some rockets down range. You can either deliver rockets in CCIP or CCRP mode. Both have their advantages and disadvantages. To most easily select rockets in CCIP mode, set the HUD as SOI and:
1. Select CCIP mode by pressing the Master Mode Control Button until selected. The current mode is displayed in the center of the HUD.
2. Press the DMS Left or Right Short until you select a rocket profile. The profile name is both listed on the DSMS Status page and in the bottom left corner of the HUD.
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Unguided Rocket Employment > Unguided Rocket CCIP Use

entries.text:
Much like the CCIP Gun Reticle, you will place the CCIP Rocket Reticle over the target by maneuvering the aircraft. When greater than 2 nm slant range, the range to target will be displayed below the reticle as a numeric. On the left side of the HUD, the projected flight time of the rocket if fired now is displayed. Horizontal Offset

The main advantage to using CCIP mode to deliver rockets is that it is more accurate than CCRP mode. The disadvantage is that it generally requires you to get closer to the target and keep your nose on it. To accurately use the CCIP rocket sight, the aircraft must know the elevation of the aim point. This is most often done by selecting DTS elevation.

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Unguided Rocket Employment > Unguided Rocket CCRP Use (1)
entries.text: CCRP rocket delivery mode allows you to launch rockets in reference to the SPI and can be done from level flight or even a lofting delivery. Before using this mode, you will first need to designate the intended target as the SPI. This could be done with the TDC, TAD, Maverick, Gun pipper or TGP. Once the target is set as SPI, select a rocket profile and set the master mode to CCRP. Upon doing so, a vertical Azimuth Steering Line (ASL) will be drawn on the HUD along the heading to the SPI. A short distance from the top of the ASL is a small circle with a dot inside called the Solution Cue.
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Unguided Rocket Employment > Unguided Rocket CCRP Use

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Unguided Rocket Employment > Unguided Rocket CCRP Use (2)
entries.text:
Also on the HUD will be the rocket reticle, but unlike CCIP mode, there will be no range numeric or analog bar.

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Unguided Rocket Employment > Unguided Rocket CCRP Use (3)
entries.text: To aim and fire rockets, you must fly the aircraft to place the rocket reticle pipper inside the small Solution Cue. In doing so, you align the aircraft along the proper heading and attitude to launch rockets for impact at the SPI location. Note that this can happen quickly, and you may need to launch several rockets in a short time before you can no longer keep the pipper in the Solution Cue. The advantage of rocket CCRP delivery is that you can engage from further way while in level flight or even pitched-up to loft rockets.
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Unguided Rocket Employment > Unguided Rocket CCRP Use

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Unguided Rocket Employment > Unguided Rocket CCRP Use (4)
entries.text: The disadvantage is that it can be much less accurate than CCIP delivery. You would generally use CCRP mode against a heavily defended target in order to suppress it.

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Unguided Rocket Employment > Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System (APKWS) (1)
entries.text:
In addition to a large selection of unguided 2.75-inch rockets, the APKWS laser-guided rocket system is also available. The APKWS, also displayed as the AGR-20A, combines a standard 2.75-inch highexplosive rocket with a laser guidance kit and control fins. There are two warhead options:
• M-151 with a high-explosive
• M-282 with a penetrator warhead From the DSMS Inventory (INV) page for ROCKETS, the laser PRF can be set. It will default to 1688, can be edited to match the targeting pod illumination PRF frequency.
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Unguided Rocket Employment > Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System (APKWS)

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Unguided Rocket Employment > Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System (APKWS) (2)
entries.text: Figure 425. APKWS DSMS Options There is no unique rocket HUD symbology for the ARG-20A other than the weapon name. The system is optimized for CCIP use, and once the designation-laser is illuminating the target on the same PRF as the APKWS, the rocket is launched as it would be for an unguided rocket. With the added laser-guidance, accuracy is significantly improved. Maximum range is between 5.0 and 6.0 nm based on launch altitude. Given the rather small size of the warhead, this weapon is best used against unarmored or lightly armored units.

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Unguided Bomb Employment > Set Up IFFCC Menu
entries.text:
If you wish to deliver an unguided bomb in CCIP mode, you have the option to do so in Manual Release (MAN REL), 3/9 Consent to Release, and 5 Mil Consent to Release (CR) modes. While Manual Release is used as the default, you can select 3/9 or 5 MIL CR from the IFFCC Test menu. To do so:
1. Place the IFFCC switch on the AHCP in the TEST position
2. With the CCIP CONSENT OPT line selected, press the DATA rocker on the UFC to cycle between the three options
3. When complete, move the IFFCC switch to the ON position

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Unguided Bomb Employment > CCIP Bombing Use
entries.text: Having configured your profile and possible inventory settings for an unguided bomb delivery, we will now discuss delivery HUD symbology and steps when using the Continuously Computed Impact Point (CCIP) weapon delivery method. We can do so in either
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Unguided Bomb Employment > CCIP Bombing Use

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Unguided Bomb Employment > CCIP Bombing Use > Manual Release (MAN REL) (1)
entries.text:
Manual release is the default release mode in CCIP and requires no change to IFFCC TEST settings. Much like rocket and gun CCIP delivery, it is a case of placing the reticle pipper over the target and then releasing the weapon. Quite simple! To deliver an unguided bomb using CCIP manual release:
1. Set the Master Arm switch on the AHCP to ARM.
2. Press the DMS Left or Right Short until the desired weapon profile is selected.
3. Press the Master Mode Control Button until CCIP is selected (as displayed in the center of the HUD).
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Unguided Bomb Employment > CCIP Bombing Use > Manual Release (MAN REL)

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Unguided Bomb Employment > CCIP Bombing Use > Manual Release (MAN REL) (2)
entries.text:
If wings level, a dashed Projected Bomb Impact Line (PBIL) will appear. You want to keep the wings as level as possible and avoid banking left and right. Doing so will cause the PBIL to swing left and right and cause a windshield wiper effect. Start a shallow dive between 10 and 45 degrees towards the intended target.

Figure 435. CCIP Bombing HUD, Out of Solution Projected Bomb Impact Line (PBIL)

Release Mode

Profile Name

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Unguided Bomb Employment > CCIP Bombing Use > Manual Release (MAN REL) (3)
entries.text: Depending on range and altitude to target, the CCIP Bombing Reticle will come into view from the bottom of the HUD and the PBIL will turn from dashed to solid. The reticle and the pipper in the center represent where the bomb(s) will drop if the weapon release button is pressed. Maneuver the aircraft to place the pipper over the target and then hold down (do not just tap) the weapon release button. If dropping multiple bombs in a ripple mode, you must hold down the weapon release button as long as it takes for all the bombs to be released.
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Unguided Bomb Employment > CCIP Bombing Use > Manual Release (MAN REL)

entries.text:
The two CR modes allow you to designate a target much as you would attack it with a CCIP Manual Release attack, and then pull up out of the attack with the target well below the HUD lower field of view. This can be a useful delivery when you want to reduce the time you are in an attack dive and it allows you to start your escape maneuver earlier. Time to Impact

entries.text: To use a CR mode, you will need to do the following: From IFFCC Test menu, select the CCIP CONSENT OPT, press the DATA rocker on the UFC to select either 3/9 or 5MIL. When you are pitched down more than 3 degrees, a dashed PBIL and reticle will appear on the HUD. The reticle with central pipper will stay clamped to the bottom of the HUD. Maneuver the aircraft to place the pipper over the intended target and then press and HOLD the weapon release button.

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Unguided Bomb Employment > CCRP Bombing Use (1)
entries.text:
Continuously Computed Release Point (CCRP) mode allows you to attack a designated ground point based on SPI location. Like CCIP, this could be done from a dive, but also from wings-level or a nosehigh attitude. To use a CCRP mode, you will need to do the following:
1. Set the Master Arm switch on the AHCP to ARM.
2. Press the DMS Left or Right Short until the desired weapon profile is selected.
3. Press the Master Mode Control Button until CCRP is selected (as displayed in the center of the HUD).
4. Set desired target as SPI.

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Laser-Guided Bomb Employment (1)
entries.text: The development of laser guided weapons has dramatically improved the accuracy of weapon guidance and delivery. With the assistance of build-up guidance kits, general GP bombs are turned into laser-guided bombs (LGBs). The kits consist of a computer- control group (CCG), guidance canards attached to the front of the warhead to provide steering commands, and a wing assembly attached to the aft end to provide lift. LGBs are maneuverable, free-fall weapons requiring no electronic interconnect to the aircraft.
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Laser-Guided Bomb Employment

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Laser-Guided Bomb Employment (2)
entries.text: They have an internal semi-active guidance system that detects laser energy and guides the weapon to a target illuminated by an external laser source. The designator can be located in the delivery aircraft, another aircraft, or a ground source. All LGB weapons have a CCG, a warhead (bomb body with fuze), and an airfoil group. The computer section transmits directional command signals to the appropriate pair(s) of canards. The guidance canards are attached to each quadrant of the control unit to change the flight path of the weapon.
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Laser-Guided Bomb Employment

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Laser-Guided Bomb Employment (3)
entries.text: The canard deflections are always full scale (referred to as “bang, bang” guidance). The LGB flight path is divided into three phases: ballistic, transition, and terminal guidance. During the ballistic phase, the weapon continues on the unguided trajectory established by the flight path of the delivery aircraft at the moment of release. In the ballistic phase, the delivery attitude takes on additional importance, since maneuverability of the UGB is related to the weapon velocity during terminal guidance.
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Laser-Guided Bomb Employment

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Laser-Guided Bomb Employment (4)
entries.text: Therefore, airspeed lost during the ballistic phase equates to a proportional loss of maneuverability. The transition phase begins at acquisition. During the transition phase, the weapon attempts to align its velocity vector with the line-of-sight vector to the target. During terminal guidance, the UGB attempts to keep its velocity vector aligned with the instantaneous line-of-sight.
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Laser-Guided Bomb Employment

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Laser-Guided Bomb Employment (5)
entries.text: At the instant alignment occurs, the reflected laser energy centers on the detector and commands the canards to a trail position, which causes the weapon to fly ballistically with gravity biasing towards the target.
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Laser-Guided Bomb Employment

3. Both the Azimuth Steering Line (ASL) and the SPI will indicate the proper heading to reach the target.

As the bomb guides to target, ensure that the targeting pod has an unobstructed line of sight to the target. Avoid any masking of the target by the aircraft. If there is masking, the M indication will be visible on the HUD.

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > IAM Bomb Employment > GBU-54A Laser-JDAM (LJDAM) (1)
entries.text: A hybrid of a GBU-38 JDAM and a GBU-12 laser-guided bomb is the GBU-54/A LJDAM. This weapon can act in both INS/GPS and laser-guidance modes, this allowing it launch-and-leave and engaging through cloud/dust as an INS/GPS weapon, and with the precision and ability to engage moving targets that laser-guidance provides. The GBU-54/A is a strap-on guidance kit for a standard Mk-82 general purpose bomb. The guidance kit includes both the GPS/INS guidance kit and a laser seeker / target detection guidance kit that allows the bomb to guide on moving targets.

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > IAM Bomb Employment > Engagement
entries.text: Upon creating the SPI at the target location, the pilot would slave the targeting pod to the SPI and laser-designate the target (static or moving) in point track or area mode. When the bomb is released, it will use GPS/INS guidance to reach the target location and the laser designation will continually update GPS/INS guidance to allow the weapon to change guidance while in flight based on the designated location. If laser-designation is lost, the weapon will continue to guide on the last designated location using INS/GPS-guidance.

entries.text: s When using the Maverick, you will use both the Maverick (MAV) MFCD page and the DSMS pages. Once the weapon has been configured, you will also use the HUD to assist in aiming. There are no IFFCC Test settings needed for the Maverick. Maverick Page All versions of the Maverick use an internal gyro to stabilize the seeker and missile before and during attack. Prior to engaging with a Maverick, you will need to align the gyros of all Mavericks loaded on the aircraft. To do so: Select the MAV display on either MFCD.

entries.text: Figure 476. Maverick in Weapon Mode, No Track With the Maverick in Weapon mode, SENSOR on the left side of the display is replaced with the Dynamic Launch Zone (DLZ). The caret on the right side of the DLZ indicates line of sight range from the aircraft to the ground point under the tracking gate. entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > AGM-65 E/O Maverick Employment > Maverick Use > Maverick in Centroid Tracking Mode (2)
entries.text: Use the slew switch or Slave All to SPI command (China Hat Forward Long) to move the tracking gate over the desired target. You can change your field of view by pressing China Hat Forward Short on the throttle. Slew the tracking gate over the target and release the slew control. When you release, the Maverick will attempt to lock onto the center of mass of a target it detects inside the tracking gate. If it cannot lock on to a target, after a few seconds, the seeker will go into Break Lock mode and the crosshairs will expand out to the edges of the display.

entries.text:
To try to lock again, slew the tracking gate back on to the target and release the slew control. Depending on the range to target and the size of the target, this may take a few tries. If the seeker is slewed from a stabilized position (boresight or slaved to SPI), it will no longer be stabilized once slewed off. Open Tracking Gate (No Locked Target)

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > AGM-65 E/O Maverick Employment > Maverick Use > Maverick in Centroid Tracking Mode (4)
entries.text:
In addition to the slew and release method of locking a target, you may also keep the tracking gate in boresight and fly to place the tracking gate over the target and then press TMS Forward Short to initiate a lock. You can also do this when the tracking gate has been moved over a target while in a slave state (such as slaving your Maverick to the SPI).

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > AGM-65 E/O Maverick Employment > Maverick Use > Maverick in Centroid Tracking Mode (5)
entries.text: When the Maverick has locked on to a target, the Pointing Cross that represents the pointing angle of the Maverick in relation to the aircraft’s longitudinal axis will flash. At this point you can hold down the weapon release button to launch the missile. If you have fired a Maverick from a LAU-88 launcher, the next Maverick on the launcher will automatically be selected and slewed to the last Maverick lock location. This is termed a “Quick Draw”.
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > AGM-65 E/O Maverick Employment > Maverick Use > Maverick in Centroid Tracking Mode

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > AGM-65 E/O Maverick Employment > Maverick Use > Maverick in Centroid Tracking Mode (6)
entries.text: If, however, you wish to select a Maverick from another station, you must cycle your profile using the HUD rotary by pressing DMS Left or Right Short. If you wish to re-cage the Maverick seeker to its boresight position or the seeker has reached its gimbal limits, you can re-cage the seeker to boresight by pressing China Hat Aft Short. Using a Maverick in centroid track is best for moving vehicles or small, stationary targets.

entries.text:
If you need to attack a specific part of a large object (such as a particular window in an office building), you can use force correlate mode with AGM/TGM-65H, AGM/TGM-65G, AGM-65K, and CATM-65K. This mode allows the seeker to create a basic picture of the scene and home in on one specified area of that scene.

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > AGM-65 E/O Maverick Employment > Maverick Use > Maverick in Force Correlate Tracking Mode (2)
entries.text:
To use the Maverick in force correlate mode:
1. Place the Boat Switch in the center position.
2. Slew the tracking gate near the intended target.
3. Ground stabilize the Maverick by pressing TMS Aft Short.
4. Slew the tracking gate over the target and the tracking gate will fully collapse. The Pointing Cross will go steady.
5. You can now launch the Maverick by holding down the weapon release button.

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > AGM-65L Laser-Guided Maverick (1)
entries.text: Unlike the other EO and IR versions of the Maverick, the AGM-65L model uses laser energy to guide on target. This laser energy can be either from the aircraft’s own LITENING pod or from an external designator like a FAC or other aircraft. However, to detect the designation, the AGM-65L needs to have its laser code set to the same PRF code as the designator. The L model has the same warhead and motor as a G model. Like an AGM-65G, it can only be mounted on the LAU-117 launcher on stations 3 and 9. It is selected in DSMS as any other Maverick type.
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > AGM-65L Laser-Guided Maverick

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > AGM-65L Laser-Guided Maverick (2)
entries.text: To include the AGM-65E, we will include a new DSMS/INVENTORY/STORE page and a new weapon video page on the selected MFCD.

entries.text:
Figure 482. AGM-65L INV Page From the DSMS/Inventory page, the laser Pulse Repetition Frequency (PRF) of the laser code the AGM-65L is programed to detected and track can be entered. To set the AGM-65L laser code using the DSMS/Inventory page:
1. Enter the four-digit, octal code on the UFC scratchpad.
2. Press the data entry option select button above the CODE selection. AGM-65L Laser Code

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > AGM-65L Laser-Guided Maverick > Laser-Maverick Video
entries.text: The AGM-65L has a free gyro assembly with a 30° field of view (up, down, left, and right). The tracker has a maximum 10° per second slew rate. The gyro takes three minutes to align, as with the other Maverick versions. Unlike the EO and IR versions of Maverick, the laser version displays a synthetic view along the longitudinal axis of the missile and only shows indications of receiving or not receiving laser energy.

When the AGM-65L is initially selected and is in “Ready” mode, the active MFCD will appear as follows with the following indications:

entries.text:
1. Laser code and cursor. The laser PRF code consists of four digits and it can be inputted using the Boat switch on the throttle (in addition to DSMS/Inventory). The default PRF code is “1 6 8 8”. The flashing horizontal line indicates the current cursor position. To use the Boat switch to enter a PRF code:
1. Move the switch forward to set the cursor under the first digit (furthest left)
2. Move the switch aft to cycle digits between 1 and 7
3. Move the switch to center to stop digit cycle
4. Move the switch forward again to move the cursor to the next digit
5.

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > AGM-65L Laser-Guided Maverick > Laser-Maverick Video > READY Mode (3)
entries.text:
Move the switch aft to cycle digits between 1 and 7
6. Repeat Once a PRF code has been set, the cursor will stop flashing. After inputting the four-digit PRF code, the user may move the cursor to the fifth position (right most) and set countermeasure mode on (when the cursor is in this position, it will not flash). This is done by cycling the Boat switch aft. When active, a “C” will be displayed.
2. Gimbal Pointing Indicator (GPI). This “X” mark indicates the pointing center of the scan. Using the slew control, the user may slew the GPI up or down to scan at a depressed angle.

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > AGM-65L Laser-Guided Maverick > Laser-Maverick Video > READY Mode (4)
entries.text:
Using a China Hat aft command, the user may reset the GPI back to center.
3. 20° hash mark. This horizontal line at the bottom of the display indicates 20° down from the center point.
4. Launch constraint circle. This is a 15° circle that indicates that maximum off boresight launch limit.
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > AGM-65L Laser-Guided Maverick > Laser-Maverick Video > READY Mode

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > AGM-65L Laser-Guided Maverick > Laser-Maverick Video > ACTIVATE Mode
entries.text: Once a PRF code has been entered, you can uncage the missile by pressing TMS forward. This is termed the “Activate” mode. Upon doing so, the seeker will begin searching for a laser designation matching that of the entered PRF code along its boresight line of sight (81 mils). If it detects laser energy along this LOS at the set PRF, the GPI will start to flash. If the reflected energy is strong enough, the flashing GPI will automatically become a solid, white square that indicates a valid lock.
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > AGM-65L Laser-Guided Maverick > Laser-Maverick Video > ACTIVATE Mode

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > AGM-65L Laser-Guided Maverick > Laser-Maverick Video > SCAN Mode
entries.text:
If a valid PRF return is not detected (non-flashing GPI), you may enter “Slew” mode. This is done by moving and releasing the slew switch. Upon doing so, the GPI will automatically scan left and right from center ±22 degrees. Using the slew switch, the user can also set the depression able that the scan will take place from.

When in Slew mode, the GPI will flash if the correct PRF code is detected. If the energy is strong enough, the GPI “X” will turn into a square and the seeker will automatically lock onto the return.
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > AGM-65L Laser-Guided Maverick > Laser-Maverick Video > SCAN Mode

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > AGM-65L Laser-Guided Maverick > Laser-Maverick Video > SLAVE Mode (1)
entries.text: In addition to manually aligning the seeker field of view with the target, you may also Slave the seeker to a SPI or TGP location within 30° of the seeker’s boresight. This is done with the slave to SPI or slave to TGP HOTAS command. When commanded, the seeker will perform an auto-track scan of the designated area and attempt to find the coded PRF. If detected (flashing GPI “X”), the user will need to manually designate with a TMS forward short HOTAS command. When slaved from another sensor, an “S” will be displayed on the right side of the display.

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System (APKWS) (1)
entries.text: The Advanced Precision Kill Weapons System (APKWS) II is a laser guidance kit developed for the Hydra 70 unguided aerial rocket. The APKWS II guidance kit consists of two forward-facing laser receivers mounted on steerable canards, turning the rocket into a precision-guided munition (PGM). APKWS II is about one-third the cost and weight of the GBU-12 500-lb. laser-guided bomb. Like the GBU-12 and other laser-guided weapons, APKWS II can be guided by the launching aircraft’s onboard laser designator, or using a laser emitted from another aircraft or ground personnel.
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System (APKWS)

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System (APKWS) (2)
entries.text: APKWS II also takes about a quarter the time of the GBU-12 to load and unload, and its low-yield warhead creates significantly reduced risk of collateral damage. The contract to develop and manufacture APKWS II was won by a partnership of BAE, Northrop Grumman, and General Dynamics. Initial operational capability (IOC) was achieved in March of 2012, and its first combat use was in early 2012, by US Marines in Afghanistan. APKWS II is mounted at the rocket mid-body. The two laser receivers work together as a single distributed-aperture semi-active laser seeker (DASALS).
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System (APKWS)

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System (APKWS) (3)
entries.text: Using laser receivers on the APKWS’s own canards simplifies installations, which does not require modification of the rocket’s nosecone. BAE describes the installation as plug and play and employment as point and shoot. The APKWS does not require any additional onboard equipment or avionics to be installed on the launching aircraft. APKWS II has an employment range of 0.5 to 2.5 nautical miles, and a guidance range of 7.5 NM. The LAU-68 F/A launch tube was lengthened to accommodate the additional 18.5 inches of length added by the guidance unit.
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System (APKWS)

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System (APKWS) (4)
entries.text: The guidance unit adds nine pounds to the rocket's overall weight. Along with the Hydra 70, APKWS II can be used on the Belgian Forges de Zeebrugge (FZ) rocket without modification. The first fixed-wing aircraft to load APKWS II was the A-10 in 2013. F-16s and A-10s both employed APKWS II during the Battle of Mosul in 2016.
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System (APKWS)

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System (APKWS) > DSMS (1)
entries.text:
On the DSMS Status page station boxes, each APKWS station consists of:
• Warhead type of M-151L high explosive warhead or M-282L penetrator warhead in top left of the box
• Alternating between APKWS and the selected laser code in the bottom left of box (XXXX)

As with other munitions, the station can be manually selected or selected via its weapon profile. In the example above, the weapon has been selected manually. Selection of the APKWS Inventory page is accessed through the Inventory → APKWS station → Rockets.

Figure 485. APKWS Status Page On the Inventory page for the APKWS, the following options are available:
• Rocket pod setting of single or double launch
• Manual laser code entry.
• Mount type of a TER or single pylon.
• Motor type of MK66 or Mk40.

• Launcher type of LAU-131 or LAU-68 (LAU-131 for the APKWS) If electing to use laser-guidance, the laser code may also be entered from the page. The default laser PRF code is 1688, but by entering a four-digit octal code on the UFC scratch pad and them pressing the LSR CODE OSB, a new code may be entered.

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System (APKWS) > Engagement (1)
entries.text: The APKWS is a laser-guided weapon system that must be supported with a laser designation from your targeting pod or an offboard designation source like a JTAC or other aircraft. Upon selecting AG mode, the APKWS weapon profile, and having the target laser-designated, you must ensure that the APKWS laser-code matches the designation laser code. At around 6 nm from the target (based on targeting pod range indication), fly to place the CCIP rocket reticle over the target area and activate the laser designation (assuming use of your targeting pod).

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Air-to-Air Employment > Using the Targeting Pod for Air-to-Air (1)
entries.text:
In addition to using your eyes to spot and track aerial targets, you can also use the targeting pod when in A-A (Air-to-Air Mode). To use the targeting pod to target aerial units, you will need to do the following:
1. Set the TGP switch on the AHCP to the ON position.
2. Select the TGP OSB from one of the MFCD to display the TGP page.
3. Once the TGP has cooled down and is displaying the default STBY (standby) page, press the A-A OSB 4. With the TGP in A-A mode, you can adjust the Field of View between Narrow and Wide by pressing China Hat Forward Short on the throttle.

If the target flies outside the crosshair area, the tracking crosshair will disappear. Select TGP A-A (Airto-Air) Mode Crosshairs Field of View Corner Markers Detect Cross

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Air-to-Air Employment > AIM/CATM-9M and 30 MM Cannon Use > Gun Use (1)
entries.text: The funnel is your gun aiming reference on the HUD and you will want to place the wing/rotor tips of the aircraft on the sides of the funnel to ensure proper angle and lead. Because the wing/rotor span can vary between aircraft, and this can lead to inaccuracy in the funnel sight, you will want to select the correct Air-to-Air Submenu (AAS) setting. With the HUD as SOI, press DMS Left or Right Short to cycle through the AAS aircraft options to match the aircraft you are engaging.
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Air-to-Air Employment > AIM/CATM-9M and 30 MM Cannon Use > Gun Use

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Air-to-Air Employment > AIM/CATM-9M and 30 MM Cannon Use > Gun Use (2)
entries.text: When you have selected the correct AAS setting and have the target within the funnel with just the wing/rotor tips touching the sides of the funnel, hold the gun trigger down. You can also use the AMIL to assist in gun aiming. This is a vertical line which represents the lead angle due to trajectory shift and gravity drop of rounds from close range out to approximately 2 seconds time of flight. The top of the AMIL shows where the bullets will be just after the firing burst and the distance they will fall towards the earth after 2 seconds due to deceleration and gravity drop. Point Track Box
entries.section: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Air-to-Air Employment > AIM/CATM-9M and 30 MM Cannon Use > Gun Use

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Air-to-Air Employment > AIM/CATM-9M and 30 MM Cannon Use > Gun Use (3)
entries.text: AIM/CATM -9M Use With an AIM/CATM-9M station selected on the DSMS, the seeker reticle will appear near the top of the HUD and represent where the seeker is currently looking. When keeping the seeker at this boresight position and maneuvering the aircraft to place the reticle over a target, you will likely hear the seeker detection or lock tone.

entries.title: COMBAT EMPLOYMENT > Air-to-Air Employment > AIM/CATM-9M and 30 MM Cannon Use > Gun Use (4)

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES (1)
entries.text:
This chapter discusses the possible emergency conditions you may encounter and how to best address them. By applying what you learn in this chapter, you should be able to ensure maximum safety for you and the aircraft. When encountering an emergency, you should always abide by the following three rules:
• Maintain aircraft control
• Analyze the situation
• Take the proper action as defined in this chapter It is important to quickly recall the following procedures by memory and use sound judgment, common sense, and a full understanding of the applicable systems.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES (2)
entries.text:
Often in this chapter we will use the terms “land as soon as possible” and “land as soon as practical”. By these terms we mean:
• Land as soon as possible. Land at the nearest suitable airfield immediately.
• Land as soon as practical. Mission should be terminated but immediate landing is not necessary.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Caution Light Panel Indications (1)
entries.text: This section discusses the possible caution light indications you may see and the corrective action to take. AIL, L/R. Either the left or right aileron has jammed. Corrective Action: Set the aileron emergency disengage switch towards the affected jam indicator light and monitor the AIL DISENG caution light. AIL DISENG. Either the left or right aileron has been disengaged from the control stick. Corrective Action: To re-engage either aileron, move the disengage switch back to center and then roll the aircraft back and forth if necessary.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Caution Light Panel Indications

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Caution Light Panel Indications (2)
entries.text: AIL TAB, L/R. This will only happen when in manual reversion mode when the roll servo tab shift actuator has been extended. Corrective Action: Exit out of manual reversion mode. ANTI-SKID. This light will illuminate when either the anti-skid switch is set to OFF while the landing gear is down, or when the switch is set to ON but there is a failure in the circuit. Corrective Action: If switch is set to OFF, set it to ON. If already on, brake carefully and avoid locking the brakes when landing. APU GEN. The APU is not generating power yet the APU generator switch is set to PWR.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Caution Light Panel Indications

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Caution Light Panel Indications (3)
entries.text:
Corrective Action: Reduce the electrical load (shut down some electrical systems) and then cycle the APU generator switch. BLEED AIR LEAK. A temperature sensor has detected bleed air leak. Corrective Action:
1. Turn the bleed air switch to OFF
2. Set APU switch to OFF
3. Land as soon as practical CADC. The Central Air Data Computer (CADC) has failed. Certain failures of the CADC can cause erroneous data to be displayed. The HUD will display the last valid airspeed and altitude data before the failure, and you will see a CADC FAIL and an INS DEGRADED message on the CDU.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Caution Light Panel Indications

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Caution Light Panel Indications (4)
entries.text: Corrective Action: Select STBY or PNEU on the altimeter and monitor pitot-static airspeed indicator. CICU. The Central Interface Control Unit (CICU) has failed. Corrective Action: Check status of CDU on CDU Systems (SYS) page. CONV, L/R. Either the left or right electrical converter has failed. Corrective Action: Land as soon as possible.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Caution Light Panel Indications

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Caution Light Panel Indications (5)
entries.text: EAC. The LASTE Enhanced Attitude Control (EAC) switch has failed. Corrective Action: Cycle the EAC button and if that fails, press the MALF button on the UFC by pressing FUNC and then CLR. ELEV, L/R. Left or right elevator has jammed. Corrective Action: Set the elevator emergency disengage switch towards the affected jam indicator light and monitor the ELEV DISENG caution light. ELEV DISENG. Either the left or right elevator has been disengaged from the control stick.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Caution Light Panel Indications

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Caution Light Panel Indications (6)
entries.text:
Corrective Action: To re-engage either elevator, move the disengage switch back to center and then pitch the aircraft up and down if necessary. ENG HOT, L/R. Either Interstage Turbine Temperature (ITT) indication is exceeding 880-c. Corrective Action: Retard throttles until ITT temperature returns to normal operating range. ENG OIL PRESS, L/R. Oil pressure in either engine falls below 34 psi. Corrective Action:
1. Set throttle of affected engine with oil problem to minimum (not IDLE)
2. If oil pressure can be maintained at 30 psi, set the affected engine throttle to IDLE
3.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Caution Light Panel Indications

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Caution Light Panel Indications (7)
entries.text: If oil pressure is still below 30 psi, set the affected engine throttle to OFF to avoid engine damage ENG START CYCLE. An engine is conducting its automatic startup cycle and the air turbine starter solenoid valve is open with the throttle at IDLE but core engine speed below 56%. This light will also illuminate when either engine operate switch is in the MOTOR position. Corrective Action: Allow engine start cycle to complete or move engine operate switch out of MOTOR position depending on engine start method. FUEL PRESS, L/R.

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Caution Light Panel Indications (8)
entries.text:
Indication of fuel pump failure due to either low differential fuel pressure or a clog in the engine feed line. Corrective Action:
1. Set the Crossfeed switch to CROSSFEED.

entries.text:

3. If still the leak continues from the left system, set the left boost pump switches to OFF. If the right system continues to leak, set the right boost pump switches to OFF and set the SAS switches to OFF. GCAS. The Ground Collision Avoidance System (GCAS) is inoperative.

Corrective Action: Set radar altimeter switch on LASTE panel to NRM and reset master caution light in UFC. GEN, L/R. Either the generators are set to OFF/RESET or there is a failure. Such a failure will also lead to the failure of the Main and Wing fuel boost pumps and SAS channels. Corrective Action:
1. If above 10,000 ft AGL, set the Crossfeed switch to CROSSFEED
2. Reset the failed generator switch back to OFF/RESET and then back to PWR
3. If after three attempts the generator does not come back online:
4. Set the failed generator back to OFF/RESET

Set APU generator switch to PWR

Corrective Action: Do not attempt to fire the gun and set the GUN/PAC and Master Arm switches on the AHCP to SAFE. HARS. HARS is offline and not providing usable data. Corrective Action: If HARS fails and is the active attitude reference source, you can restore yaw dampening and trim by:
• EGI is operating:
1. Select EGI on the Navigation Mode Select Panel
2. Reengage the YAW SAS channels

entries.text:
Mode-4 is inoperative due to IFF panel being zeroized or system failure. Corrective Action: Set correct mode or exit interrogation environment. INST INV. Instrument inverter switch is inoperative and indicates no power is being provided to the AC essential busses. This is indicative of the loss of both AC generators. Such a condition will also lead to the L and R ENG HOT caution lights illuminating. Corrective Action:
1. Engine core speeds should be below 90% when below 25,000 MSL and 85% when above 25,000 MSL
2. Cycle Inverter switch between TEST and STBY and then leave in STBY
3.

entries.text:
Start APU when below 15,000 MSL
4. Set the APU generator switch to PWR
5. Land as soon as practical L-R TKS UNEQUAL. An imbalance of greater than 750 lbs. of fuel between the two main fuselage tanks has been detected. Corrective Action:
1. Set the Crossfeed switch to CROSSFEED on the Fuel Control panel

entries.text:
2. Set wing boost pumps to OFF
3. If right system has less fuel: set right main boost pump switch to OFF
4. If left system has less fuel: set left main boost pump switch to OFF LASTE. The Low Altitude Safety and Targeting Enhancement (LASTE) system is inoperative. Corrective Action: Cycle the IFFCC switch on the AHCP. MAIN FLOW LOW, L/R. Fuel quantity is below 500 lbs. Corrective Action: Land as soon as possible. MAIN PUMP, L/R. entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Caution Light Panel Indications (19)
entries.text: Corrective Action: Failure of either main boost pump will illuminate the MAIN PUMP, L or R caution lights. Assuming wing boost pumps are still operating, the engines will still be provided fuel due to that pressure. If both main and wing boost pumps are not working though, suction-feed will supply the engines below 10,000 ft. Above this altitude, engine operation may suffer. In this event, set the Crossfeed switch to CROSSFEED. If this causes rapid fuel transfer between tanks, pull all Fill Disable switches. NAV.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Caution Light Panel Indications

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Caution Light Panel Indications (20)
entries.text:
There are multiple reasons this light may illuminate and most of them involve EGI state. Possible reasons for this caution and corrective actions include:
• EGI flight instrument failure
1. Set the Navigation Mode Select Panel to HARS from EGI
2. Verify an EGI FLY INST FAIL message on the CDU
3. From the RESET page of the CDU, select the EGI line select key
• EGI is not ready failure
1. Verify EGI switch is set to ON on the AAP
2. Set the EGI switch to OFF for at least 10 seconds
3. Reset the EGI switch back to ON
• EGI GPS failure
1. On the CDU, verify a GPS FAIL message
2.

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Caution Light Panel Indications (21)
entries.text:
On the Navigation Mode Select Panel, ensure EGI is selected
3. From the CDU RESET page, press the REINIT INS line select key, if failure persists…
4. On the Navigation Mode Select Panel, select HARS

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Caution Light Panel Indications (22)
entries.text:
5. On the CDU REINIT page, press the REINIT GPS line select key
• EGI INS failure
1. On the CDU, verify an INS FAIL message
2. On the Navigation Mode Select Panel, ensure EGI is selected
3. From the CDU RESET page, press the EGI line select key, if failure persists: 3.1. On the Navigation Mode Select Panel, select HARS 3.2. On the CDU REINIT page, press the REINIT GPS line select key
• CDU failure
1. On the AAP, set the CDU switch to OFF for at least 4 seconds
2. Set the CDU switch back to the ON position. If the problem persists: 2.1. Reload DTS data 2.2.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Caution Light Panel Indications

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Caution Light Panel Indications (23)
entries.text: Select desired Navigation Mode Select Panel settings OXY LOW. 0.5 liter or less of liquid oxygen remains in oxygen converters. Corrective Action: Descend below 10,000 ft AGL and land as soon as practical. PITCH SAS. One or both SAS channels have been disengaged. Corrective Action: Reengage one channel at a time and if both cannot be reengaged, leave both off. Avoid single-channel operation as it can result in undesired loading on the interconnector shear bolts. SEAT NOT ARMED. Seat ground safety lever in SAFE position. Corrective Action: N/A SERVICE AIR HOT.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Caution Light Panel Indications

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Caution Light Panel Indications (24)
entries.text:
Indication of excessive pre-cooler output air temperature. Corrective Action:
1. Turn the bleed air switch to OFF
2. Set APU switch to OFF
3. Land as soon as practical STALL SYS. There has been a failure in the alpha/Mach computer and the stall warning will be inoperative. In such a situation, the slats extend automatically. Corrective Action: Do not exceed 20 units of AoA.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Caution Light Panel Indications

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Caution Light Panel Indications (25)
entries.text: WINDSHIELD HOT. Windshield anti-icing temperature is in excess of 150-F or aircraft is on battery electrical power only. Corrective Action: N/A WING PUMP, L/R. Indication of possible fuel boost pump failure due to fuel pressure differential at outlet of indicated wing fuel boost pump is low. Corrective Action: If the L or R WING BOOST PUMP caution lights illuminate, it indicates the fuel in the tank of the boost pump will not transfer until the amount is below 600 lb. If left unchecked, this can lead to a weight imbalance.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Caution Light Panel Indications

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Caution Light Panel Indications (26)
entries.text: To remedy, select CROSSFEED from the Crossfeed switch on the Fuel panel. This will allow the tanks to equalize and maintain fuel balance. If, however, there is too rapid fuel transfer between tanks, you can pull the All Fill Disable switches. YAW SAS. One or both YAW SAS channels have been disengaged. Corrective Action: Reengage one channel at a time and if both cannot be reengaged, leave both off. Avoid single-channel operation as it can result in undesired loading on the interconnector shear bolts.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Caution Light Panel Indications

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Caution Light Panel Indications (27)
entries.text: On the Navigation Mode Select Panel, cycle between HARS and EGI to reset the attitude reference system and then attempt to reengage the channels.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Caution Light Panel Indications

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Flight and Flight Control Emergencies > Flap Asymmetry
entries.text:
If the flaps fail to extend or retract symmetrically, you should attempt the following remedies in order:
1. Re-select the flap position at which the asymmetry first occurred. If that does not work: 1.1. Set flaps to MVR setting when speed and altitude allow. If that does not work: 1.1.1. On the Emergency Flight Control Panel, enable the FLAP EMER RETR switch by moving the switch up.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Flight and Flight Control Emergencies > Flap Asymmetry

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Flight and Flight Control Emergencies > Speed Brake Asymmetry or Failure
entries.text: On the Emergency Flight Control Panel, move the SPD BK EMER RETR switch up to close.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Flight and Flight Control Emergencies > Speed Brake Asymmetry or Failure

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Flight and Flight Control Emergencies > Aileron/Elevator Jam
entries.text: Indicated by either a AIL, L/R or ELEV, L/R caution panel light, one or more aileron or elevator control surfaces have jammed. Disengage the control and allow normal movement of the controls, move the emergency disengage switch on the Emergency Flight Control Panel in the direction of the jam indicator light.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Flight and Flight Control Emergencies > Aileron/Elevator Jam

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Flight and Flight Control Emergencies > Hydraulic Failure (1)
entries.text: The aircraft has both left and right hydraulic systems and the failure of one still allows adequate flight control response. Failure of either the systems can be indicated by the L and R HYD RES (hydraulic fluid reservoir low) caution light or the L and R HYD PRESS (hydraulic pressure low) caution light. However, the loss of one hydraulic system will reduce rudder authority.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Flight and Flight Control Emergencies > Hydraulic Failure

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Flight and Flight Control Emergencies > Hydraulic Failure (2)
entries.text:
If the left hydraulic system fails, you will lose the following systems:
• Flaps
• Nosewheel steering
• Normal landing gear operation
• Wheel brakes
• Anti-skid
• Hydraulic control of the left elevator and rudder actuators
• Loss of dual channel pitch and yaw SAS If left system fails:
1. Set the FLAP EMER RETR switch to EMER RETR on the Emergency Flight Control Panel.
2. If pressure continues to decrease: 2.1. Set the SAS/Anti-skid paddle to OFF 2.2. Keep Pitch SAS OFF 2.3.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Flight and Flight Control Emergencies > Hydraulic Failure

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Flight and Flight Control Emergencies > Hydraulic Failure (3)
entries.text:
Land as soon as possible If the right hydraulic system fails, you will lose the following systems:
• Slats (will extend with loss of hydraulic power)
• Air refueling slipway and nozzle hatch rollers
• Speed brakes
• Right elevator and rudder actuators
• Loss of dual channel pitch and yaw SAS If right system fails:
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Flight and Flight Control Emergencies > Hydraulic Failure

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Flight and Flight Control Emergencies > Hydraulic Failure (4)
entries.text:
1. Set the SP BK EMER RETR switch to EMER RETR on the Emergency Flight Control Panel.
2. If pressure continues to decrease: 2.1. Set the SAS/Anti-skid paddle to OFF 2.2. Keep Pitch SAS OFF 2.3. Enable Anti-skid if left hydraulic system is still operable 2.4. Land as soon as possible If both systems fail:
1. Maintain 1G flight between 180 and 210 KIAS
2. Set flaps to full UP (use emergency retract if needed)
3. Jettison stores to produce symmetrical loading
4. Enable Manual Reversion Mode
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Flight and Flight Control Emergencies > Hydraulic Failure

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Flight and Flight Control Emergencies > Trim Failure
entries.text: If the normal aircraft trim system fails, set the PITCH/ROLL TRIM switch to EMER OVERRIDE on the Emergency Flight Control Panel and then use the emergency pitch and roll trim switch to set desired trim.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Flight and Flight Control Emergencies > Trim Failure

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Flight and Flight Control Emergencies > Out-of-Control Recovery
entries.text:
If the aircraft departs from controlled flight as the result of an un-commanded roll reversal or spin, it can be easily recovered from after a few control oscillations. To recover:
1. Neutralize all controls until oscillations have ceased. Trying to rush the recovery may only exacerbate the problem.
2. Set throttles to IDLE.
3. If in a spin, full input of rudder opposite of turn needle. Note that a spin can take between 4,000 and 10,000 feet to recover from depending on severity.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Flight and Flight Control Emergencies > Out-of-Control Recovery

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Flight and Flight Control Emergencies > Hypoxia
entries.text:
If you are not receiving enough oxygen above 20,000 ft MSL, you may suffer the effects of hypoxia and lose consciousness. If you start to see visual effects, you must ensure:
• Oxygen lever is set to ON.
• Oxygen flow indicator is blinking.
• Oxygen pressure is above 55 psi.

If set correctly and effects are still present, descend below 13,000 ft.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Flight and Flight Control Emergencies > Hypoxia

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Flight and Flight Control Emergencies > Manual Reversion Landing (1)
entries.text:
When landing in Manual Reversion Flight Control System (MRFCS) mode, the landing should only be attempted in ideal conditions and flight controls should not be degraded, maximum allowed crosswind is 20 knots, no ECM pods can be loaded on stations 1 and 11, and you must never use pitch trim for flaring the aircraft. If you cannot meet these conditions, you should eject from the aircraft. To perform an MRFCS landing:
1. Jettison external fuel tanks.
2. Extend landing gear either normally or with AUX LG EXT handle.
3. Pull the EMER BRAKE handle.
4.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Flight and Flight Control Emergencies > Manual Reversion Landing

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Flight and Flight Control Emergencies > Manual Reversion Landing (2)
entries.text:
Fly a straight in approach at 1.5 to 2 degrees with low sink rate.
5. When below 50 ft AGL, pitch response becomes degraded.
6. Maintain minimum airspeed around 140 KIAS to touchdown.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Flight and Flight Control Emergencies > Manual Reversion Landing

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Engine, APU, and Fuel Emergencies > Engine Fire
entries.text:
If an engine fire is detected in either engine, the engine fire right or left T-Handle will illuminate. In case of such a fire, follow these steps:
1. Reduce power to affected engine and monitor if the fire light goes out. If the fire persists: 1.1. Set the throttle of the affected engine to OFF. 1.2. Pull the fire T-Handle of the affected engine. 1.3. Press the fire discharge agent switch left or right. 1.4. If both presses of the discharge agent switch fail to put out the fire, land as soon as possible.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Engine, APU, and Fuel Emergencies > Engine Fire

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Engine, APU, and Fuel Emergencies > APU Fire
entries.text:
If an APU fire is detected, the APU fire T-Handle will illuminate. This will likely be accompanied with a Bleed Air Leak caution light. In case of such a fire, follow these steps:
1. If the APU is operating, set the APU switch to OFF. If the fire persists:

1.1. Pull the fire T-Handle of the APU. 1.2. Press the fire discharge agent switch left or right. 1.3. If both presses of the discharge agent switch fail to put out the fire, land as soon as possible.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Engine, APU, and Fuel Emergencies > APU Fire

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Engine, APU, and Fuel Emergencies > Single Engine Restart (1)
entries.text:
If an engine needs to be restarted while in flight you can either use the APU to restart the engine or perform a windmill air start. APU Restart. Using the APU to restart an engine is performed as follows:
1. Move the inoperative engine throttle to the OFF position.
2. Observe that the shut-down engine ITT value cools down rapidly.
3. Aircraft altitude should be below 20,000 ft MSL and increase airspeed.
4. When below 15,000 ft MSL, move the APU power switch to the START position.
5. Move the still operating throttle to MAX.
6.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Engine, APU, and Fuel Emergencies > Single Engine Restart

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Engine, APU, and Fuel Emergencies > Single Engine Restart (2)
entries.text:
Set the Engine Operate switch of the affected engine to the MOTOR setting.
7. When affected engine ITT is below 100°C and altitude below 15,000 ft MSL, restart the affected engine by moving the throttle from OFF to IDLE.
8. Move the Engine Operate switch of the affected engine back to the NORM position.
9. If engine restart is successful, reengage the SAS switches. Windmill Restart. Using a windmill start will take 6,000 to 8,000 ft to complete because it requires a steep dive of at least 30°. Given the altitude requirement, this is not an option when below 10,000 ft AGL.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Engine, APU, and Fuel Emergencies > Single Engine Restart

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Engine, APU, and Fuel Emergencies > Single Engine Restart (3)
entries.text:
To perform a windmill restart:
1. Place the aircraft in a 30° dive.
2. Set the Bleed Air switch to OFF.
3. Set the Crossfeed switch to Crossfeed.
4. Once ITT of affected engine is below 150-c, set both throttles to MAX.
5. Set the Engine Operate switch of the affected engine to IGN.
6. Once engine is operating, move Engine Operate switch back to NORM.
7. Move Crossfeed switch to OFF.
8. Set Bleed Air switch to ON.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Engine, APU, and Fuel Emergencies > Single Engine Restart

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Engine, APU, and Fuel Emergencies > Engine Start after a Failed Start (1)
entries.text: If an engine fails to start using the automatic NORM mode, the engine combustion chamber may be flooded with fuel and needs to be purged before it can be restarted or risk a hot start. A failed start
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Engine, APU, and Fuel Emergencies > Engine Start after a Failed Start

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Engine, APU, and Fuel Emergencies > Engine Start after a Failed Start (2)
entries.text:
can happen if you fail to set the Inverter switch to STBY, causing the inverters to fail to provide power to the engine igniters. To purge an engine of fuel:
1. Set the Throttle of the affected engine to OFF.
2. Set the Engine Operate switch of the affected engine to the MOTOR position for 30 seconds. After completing the purge, you can attempt to restart the engine after correcting what prevented the engine from starting earlier.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Engine, APU, and Fuel Emergencies > Engine Start after a Failed Start

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Engine, APU, and Fuel Emergencies > APU Over-temperature
entries.text: If the APU temperature begins to fluctuate or experiences an over-temperature, you need to shut it down immediately by setting the APU power switch to OFF. If airborne, land as soon as practical. If however the APU is needed for engine start or electrical power, you can try to restart the APU and closely monitor it. Avoid running the APU when one or both engines are running above 80% core RPM as a bleed air failure can cause aircraft damage.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Engine, APU, and Fuel Emergencies > APU Over-temperature

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Engine, APU, and Fuel Emergencies > Engine Oil Malfunction
entries.text:
If the oil pressure for either engine is outside its normal operating limits, you need to take the following steps:
1. Set throttle of affected engine with oil problem to minimum (not IDLE).
2. If oil pressure can be maintained at 30 psi, set the affected engine throttle to IDLE.
3. If oil pressure is still below 30 psi, set the affected engine throttle to OFF to avoid engine damage.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Engine, APU, and Fuel Emergencies > Engine Oil Malfunction

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Engine, APU, and Fuel Emergencies > Main Fuel Boost Pump Failure
entries.text: Failure of either main boost pump will illuminate the MAIN PUMP, L or R caution lights. Assuming wing boost pumps are still operating, the engines will still be provided fuel due to that pressure. If both main and wing boost pumps are not working though, suction-feed will supply the engines below 10,000 ft. Above this altitude, engine operation may suffer. In this event, set the Crossfeed switch to CROSSFEED. If this causes rapid fuel transfer between tanks, pull the Fill Disable switches.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Engine, APU, and Fuel Emergencies > Main Fuel Boost Pump Failure

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Engine, APU, and Fuel Emergencies > Wing Fuel Boost Pump Failure
entries.text:
If the L or R WING BOOST PUMP caution lights illuminate, it indicates the fuel in the tank of the boost pump will not transfer until the amount is below 600 lb. If left unchecked, this can lead to a weight imbalance. To remedy, select CROSSFEED from the Crossfeed switch on the Fuel panel. This

will allow the tanks to equalize and maintain fuel balance. If however there is too rapid of a fuel transfer between tanks, you can pull the Fill Disable switches.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Engine, APU, and Fuel Emergencies > Wing Fuel Boost Pump Failure

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Engine, APU, and Fuel Emergencies > Fuel Pressure Low or Fuel Leak (1)
entries.text: This is indicated by either the L-FUEL PRESS or R-FUEL PRESS caution lights illuminating. If either light illuminates, set the Crossfeed switch to the CROSSFEED position. If this does not extinguish the light(s), set the Crossfeed switch back to OFF and monitor fuel quantity to determine if a leak exists. If it appears a leak does exist, set the affected engine throttle to OFF and pull the fire T-handle of the affected engine. If the leak still continues from the left system, set the left boost pump switches to OFF.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Engine, APU, and Fuel Emergencies > Fuel Pressure Low or Fuel Leak

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Engine, APU, and Fuel Emergencies > Fuel Pressure Low or Fuel Leak (2)
entries.text: If the right system continues to leak, set the right boost pump switches to OFF and set the SAS switches to OFF.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Engine, APU, and Fuel Emergencies > Fuel Pressure Low or Fuel Leak

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Emergency Landings and Exiting > Single Engine Landing (1)
entries.text:
When one of the engines has failed and a safe, controlled flight is still possible, a landing can still be performed using the following guidance:
1. Ensure the failed engine will cause no damage to the aircraft due to fire.
2. Use the rudders to compensate for yaw due to single engine operation. If possible, bank into the direction of the operating engine.
3. Advance the operating engine throttle to MAX.
4. Close speedbrakes if open.
5. Set flaps to MVR setting.
6. A straight in approach should be used and all set up maneuvering completed 2 to 3 nm from touchdown point.
7.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Emergency Landings and Exiting > Single Engine Landing

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Emergency Landings and Exiting > Single Engine Landing (2)
entries.text:
If level flight with maximum power cannot be maintained, external stores should be jettisoned.
8. Lower the landing gear and compensate for increased drag.
9. Reduce power slowly during landing flare with careful and coordinated rudder input to keep aircraft aligned down the runway.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Emergency Landings and Exiting > Single Engine Landing

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Emergency Landings and Exiting > Flameout Landing (1)
entries.text:
If an ejection is not possible, a flameout landing should be attempted. A flameout landing is when both engines are not producing any thrust and you must land.

Figure 494. Flameout Approach Enter landing pattern with a very steep approach using a circular pattern which will result in a low displacement 8,000 ft from the runway. All turns within the pattern should be limited to 30° of bank.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Emergency Landings and Exiting > Flameout Landing

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Emergency Landings and Exiting > Flameout Landing (2)
entries.text: Lower landing gear with a minimum airspeed of 160 KIAS. Altitude should be between 7,000 and 6,500 ft AGL. Maintain 160 KIAS and altitude should be between 3,500 and 4,000 ft AGL. On the base leg, maintain 160 KIAS and an altitude of between 2,000 and 2,500 ft AGL. Roll out on final should be initiated early due to the slow roll response of the aircraft if in manual reversion mode. Final approach will have aircraft at 150 KIAS wings level above 500 ft AGL. Touchdown should occur 1/3 down the runway. The landing flare should be done at 120 KIAS when 200 to 300 ft AGL over the runway.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Emergency Landings and Exiting > Flameout Landing

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Emergency Landings and Exiting > Flameout Landing (3)
entries.text: When 50 ft AGL, shallow the flight path to 1.5 to 2 degrees. Note that pitch response will be greatly degraded when below 50 ft AGL due to the ground effect. Once on the ground, emergency brakes should be used because no anti-skid, flaps, or speed brakes will be available.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Emergency Landings and Exiting > Flameout Landing

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Emergency Landings and Exiting > Landing Gear Extension Failure (1)
entries.text:
Ideally, you always want to land with all three landing gears extended and locked with three green gear-down indicators on the landing gear panel. If moving the landing gear handle to the down position does not result in three down and locked lights, you should try the following:
1. Press the Signal Lights button to make sure the lights are operating.
2. Check that there is pressure in the left hydraulic system. If pressure looks good…
3. Cycle the landing gear handle back up and then down again.
4. Increase airspeed to 200 KIAS and pitch and roll the aircraft to shake loose the gear.
5.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Emergency Landings and Exiting > Landing Gear Extension Failure

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Emergency Landings and Exiting > Landing Gear Extension Failure (2)
entries.text:
If all this fails, use the Landing Gear Alternative Extension Handle. To use this handle:
6. Reduce airspeed below 200 KIAS
7. Ensure landing gear handle is down
8. Pull AUX LG EXT handle along the lower left side of the center dash
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Emergency Landings and Exiting > Landing Gear Extension Failure

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Emergency Landings and Exiting > No Gear Down or Partial Gear Down Landings (1)
entries.text:
If you are unable to lower the landing gear as described above, you will need to perform a wheels-up landing. To perform a wheels-up landing, follow these steps:
1. Push in the AUX LG EXT handle.
2. Jettison all stores and flares.
3. Burn off excess fuel.
4. Pull the EMER BRAKE.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Emergency Landings and Exiting > No Gear Down or Partial Gear Down Landings

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Emergency Landings and Exiting > No Gear Down or Partial Gear Down Landings (2)
entries.text:
5. Set speed brakes to 40%.
6. Lower flaps to 20°.
7. Fly shallow approach at 2° at normal airspeed.
8. Touchdown at a minimum sink rate on center of runway.
9. After touchdown, open speed brakes to full.
10. Reduce throttles to IDLE.
11. Move control stick to full aft.
12. Once you have come to a stop, set the throttles to OFF.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Emergency Landings and Exiting > No Gear Down or Partial Gear Down Landings

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Emergency Landings and Exiting > Ejection (1)
entries.text:
Using the ejection seat, you can exit the aircraft at most any speed and altitude, but ejection above 2,000 ft AGL wings level is preferable. If below 2,000 ft AGL, do not delay in making the decision. If in uncontrolled flight, eject at an altitude above 4,000 ft AGL. If time permits, the following steps should be taken before ejecting from the aircraft:
1. Set IFF panel to EMER and set appropriate Mode 3/A code.
2. Transmit “May Day” call on UHF guard channel.
3. Turn aircraft to uninhabited area.
4. Trim aircraft for lowest practical speed with wings level.
5.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Emergency Landings and Exiting > Ejection

entries.title: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Emergency Landings and Exiting > Ejection (2)
entries.text: When ready to eject, pull either ejection handle, and the process will start immediately.
entries.section: EMERGENCY PROCEDURES > Emergency Landings and Exiting > Ejection
